{{Short description|German mathematician}}
[[File:Uwe Storch.jpg|thumb|220px|Uwe Storch]]
'''Uwe Storch''' (born 12 July 1940, [[Staßfurt|Leopoldshall]]&ndash; [[Lanzarote]], 17 September 2017) was a [[Germany|German]] [[mathematician]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Uwe Storch |url=https://www.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/ffm/Lehrstuehle/Storch/Storch.html |access-date=2025-08-30 |website=www.ruhr-uni-bochum.de}}</ref> His field of research was [[commutative algebra]], and [[analytic geometry|analytic]] and [[algebraic geometry]], in particular [[derivation (abstract algebra)|derivation]]s, [[divisor class group]], and [[resultant]]s.

Storch studied [[mathematics]], [[physics]], and [[mathematical logic]] at the [[University of Münster]] and [[Heidelberg University]]. He got his PhD in 1966 under the supervision of [[Heinrich Behnke]] with a [[thesis]] on almost (or Q) [[factorial]] [[Ring (mathematics)|rings]]. He did his [[Habilitation]] in 1972 in [[Bochum]] and became a professor at the [[Osnabrück University|University of Osnabrück]] in 1974. From 1981 to 2006, when he became emeritus, he was a professor for algebra and geometry at [[Ruhr University Bochum]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Flenner |first=Hubert |date=December 8, 2010 |title=Uwe Storch's Mathematical Work |url=https://www.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/imperia/md/content/mathematik/lehrstuhli/_bangalore.pdf}}</ref>

He was married and had four sons.

==Theorem of Eisenbud–Evans–Storch==

The [[Theorem]] of [[David Eisenbud|Eisenbud]]-[[Graham Evans (mathematician)|Evans]]-Storch states that
every [[algebraic variety]] in n-[[dimension]]al [[affine space]]
is given geometrically (i.e. up to [[radical of an ideal|radical]]) by n [[polynomial]]s.

==Selected publications==
Günther Scheja and Uwe Storch, ''Lehrbuch der Algebra'', 2 volumes, Stuttgart 1980 (1st edition was in 3 volumes), 1988.

Uwe Storch and Hartmut Wiebe, ''Lehrbuch der Mathematik'', 4 volumes.
